page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. This KVM-hypervised instance features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the instance delivers modest processing capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the server in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% categories, respectively. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block memory write bandwidth achieves an average rating, read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains in the bottom 25%. Computational tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show poor single-threaded performance, though multi-threaded decompression and Passmark CPU extended instructions reach average tiers.

Given the high memory capacity of 64.0 GB relative to its 8 vCPUs, the server is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput. It is suitable for caching layers, lightweight database operations, and small-scale language model inference, where it achieves average performance processing 135M parameter models. However, the lack of local storage and weak CPU performance make it less suitable for high-throughput static web serving, large-scale software compilation, or complex mathematical simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, this KVM-based instance provides 8.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks indicate modest CPU capabilities, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores generally falling into the bottom 25% tier. However, the instance maintains average performance in large-block memory write bandwidth and small-scale LLM inference. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy, compute-light workloads. It is best suited for caching, lightweight database tasks, and basic text processing rather than CPU-intensive compilation or high-throughput web serving.
